releases.notes:
- System -> Console settings -> Screen brightness: pick Custom and choose with two bars how dark and how bright the screens can get. The console's five levels are spread between them.
- It works in every game and in HOME, with auto-brightness too, so it no longer gets too dark. It stays after NSA closes, and System puts the console's own levels back.
- A new chapter of the guide, Screen brightness, shows where it is and how it works.

- Titles: the console's own software is marked in red ("System" in the list, a red dot on the grid), and deleting one first says what it is and that the console may not start without it, then asks again with A on Cancel: X deletes.
- Files: the actions of the folder you are in (X) have a header in the accent colour with the folder's whole path, and the list behind shows no item selected, so they can't be taken for the selected item's actions.

- Store: "Remove what the Store installed" takes away what an app's downloads put on the SD card (texture packs, mods, plugins...), wherever its steps put them. The Store notes every file it writes as it installs, so it removes exactly those.
- It asks first and says how many files and where. Files that replaced others that were already there are pointed out (deleting them doesn't bring the old ones back), files changed since are left, and the folders left empty go.
- It works for what is installed from this version on, and keeps no copies: nothing extra on the SD card.

- A store's "Send to 3DS" button, such as Brewology's "Send to 3dsDL", now sends straight to NSA: links to http://3ds.local/ (or nsa.local) reach the console while NSA is open.
- Nothing downloads until you answer on the console, and the question says which device and which website the links come from.
- From a phone or a computer on your Wi-Fi, open http://3ds.local/ to paste links; the page is in the console's language.
- Settings -> Links from web pages turns it off.

- Send several titles to another 3DS at once: mark them in Titles (the tick icon at the top) and press START. The other console accepts them all with one answer and picks for each one, from its free space, whether it installs as it arrives or as a package.
- Titles: holding A with titles marked offers what can be done to all of them: send them, export them as CIAs or delete them.
- Download queue: downloads go on in the background, one after another, from the Store or Install from URL. Pause, resume or reorder them from its icon in the main menu or from the web page.
- Store: an app's pictures, and Uninstall the CIA / Delete the 3DSX for what the Store installed.
- Archives: View contents shows what a zip holds, and Install from URL and Remote install extract it into place on the SD card (an app into /3ds/<app>/).
- Every screen's buttons stay readable at the bottom, and the (i) at its left lists them all.

- Settings -> Changelog shows the notes in your language, one release per page: L / R turn pages, ZL / ZR go to the first or the last, and the bottom screen lists every release to jump to one.
- Store: all 448 Universal-DB apps are offered, as in Universal-Updater. Apps that write to boot.firm, /luma, /gm9 or /private (Luma3DS, GodMode9, plugin frameworks...) show a red warning first, and so do downloads over plain http.
- Store: an app's other options can now remove what they installed (such as a patch's "Remove the patch"), and entries with no file say there is nothing to download.
- Settings and the menus keep moving after a flick and have the round arrows (and ZL / ZR on a New 3DS) to jump to the top or the end.
- Bug reports and ideas on GitHub now start from a form.

- Lists open at the top while they load and sort; floating arrows (and ZL / ZR on a New 3DS) jump to the start or the end.
- Your own themes: Settings -> Edit the theme changes every colour with a finger and shows it at once on both screens, from any theme or a blank template; the web page has the same editor. They are kept as files in /nsa/themes/.
- HOME theme: icon grids in pages that turn sideways (tap a dot, or drag the bar, to jump to one), and sheets close when pulled down.
- Pixel theme: the digits, B and Z are drawn by hand, so 5 and S, 8 and B no longer look alike.
- New guide chapter: Your own themes.

- A .3dsx can be installed in the HOME Menu (SD card, the .3dsx's actions, "Install in the HOME Menu"): it becomes a real title, not a forwarder, so it starts and quits like any other and the .3dsx is no longer needed.
- Its icon and name come from the .3dsx; the banner is drawn from them, or made from a picture of yours.
- Installing the same .3dsx again updates the title; a newer .3dsx needs to be installed again to update it.

- System is now three groups: Information (console, network, storage, battery), Console settings (Date and time, Wi-Fi connections) and Hardware tests.
- Buttons and touch: every key, the Circle Pad, the C-Stick, the touch screen and the 3D and volume sliders, live, with a counter of what is left to try and a magnified view of each stick's centre to spot drift.
- Motion sensors: the accelerometer and the gyroscope live, and a recording of both to a CSV file in /nsa/logs that keeps going with the lid closed.
- Guide: a chapter for the hardware tests, and the Wi-Fi and Date and time tours go through Console settings.

- Web interface PIN (Settings -> Web PIN): a new random one at each start (as before), a fixed one you type on a numeric keypad or make random, or none. When a browser asks for the PIN, the console shows it at the bottom of the screen.
- Remote install: two small buttons beside History turn the FTP server and the web server on or off, and show their address (the web one also its PIN and a QR code). History shows the last file's name.
- NSA's own boot logo when it starts from the HOME menu (the installed CIA), with a day and a night look.
- Titles: "Extract ExeFS" copies a title's code, icon, banner and logo to the SD card.
- FTP: Dolphin and other file managers that open several connections browse without hanging (5 sessions, a single file in a listing, a longer wait for data connections).
- Guide: new steps for all this, and the Wi-Fi tour no longer gets stuck when A is pressed on another row.
